title: 05_bidbarn_refunds
summary: This document explains how refunds work on BidBarn, including when you can get money back and that digital purchases can’t be refunded once you open them. It says the seller, not BidBarn, is responsible for any problems, and that a monthly Seller Pro subscription renews automatically unless you cancel. The refund rules can change at any time, so you should check them often.
keyPoints: You can only get a refund for shipped items if they’re damaged and you report it within 48 hours.
Opening a digital download means you can’t get a refund.
The seller, not BidBarn, is responsible for any issues with the sale.
Monthly Seller Pro subscriptions keep charging you until you cancel them.
BidBarn may change the refund rules at any time, so review them regularly.

risks.clauseQuote: For digital items, all sales are final and no refunds are given once the download link has been opened.
risks.explanation: If you open the download, you lose the right to a refund, even if you change your mind.

risks.clauseQuote: Monthly subscription fees for BidBarn Seller Pro renew automatically until cancelled.
risks.explanation: The company will keep charging you each month unless you actively cancel the subscription.

risks.clauseQuote: Once an order has shipped, refunds are only available for items that arrive damaged, and you must report damage within 48 hours of delivery.
risks.explanation: If you wait too long after delivery, you won’t get your money back unless the item is damaged and you report it quickly.

risks.clauseQuote: BidBarn is not a party to the sale contract between you and the seller.
risks.explanation: If something goes wrong, BidBarn won’t be responsible for fixing it; you have to deal directly with the seller.

risks.clauseQuote: We may change these refund rules at any time by posting the updated version on this page.
risks.explanation: The rules can be altered whenever the site updates, so what’s true today might change later without you being directly notified.

disclaimer: This is an automated plain-language summary, not legal advice. Check the original document for anything that matters to you.
